rules.name: Docker disk image
rules.what: The single disk file Docker Desktop keeps your images, containers and volumes in. Volumes can hold databases, so Leftover never moves this file. Use Docker's own commands to see and reclaim space inside it.

rules.name: Docker data
rules.what: Where Docker Engine keeps images, containers, volumes and build cache on Linux. Volumes can hold databases, so Leftover never moves this folder. Its size comes from Docker itself, since the folder belongs to root.

rules.name: OrbStack data
rules.what: OrbStack's disk image, holding your Docker images, containers, volumes and Linux machines. Leftover never moves it. Use Docker's own commands to reclaim space inside it.

rules.name: Colima VMs
rules.what: The virtual machines Colima runs Docker in, with their disks. Your images, containers and volumes live inside. Leftover never moves them.

rules.name: Playwright browsers
rules.what: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit builds Playwright downloaded for testing. Each Playwright upgrade adds new ones.
rules.comeback: Run npx playwright install to download the versions your project needs.

rules.name: Puppeteer browsers
rules.what: Chrome builds Puppeteer downloaded when it was installed.
rules.comeback: Run npx puppeteer browsers install chrome, or reinstall the package.

rules.name: Cypress binaries
rules.what: Cypress app versions downloaded by your projects. Old versions are never removed on their own.
rules.comeback: npx cypress install downloads the version a project needs.

rules.name: Electron downloads
rules.what: Electron releases downloaded when installing Electron apps you are developing.
rules.comeback: Downloaded again the next time a project installs Electron.

rules.name: JetBrains IDE caches
rules.what: Indexes and caches for each JetBrains IDE version. Folders for versions you no longer use stay behind after every upgrade.
rules.comeback: The IDE rebuilds its indexes the next time it opens a project. Your settings live elsewhere and aren't touched.

rules.name: VS Code caches
rules.what: VS Code's compiled code cache and copies of extension installers. VS Code doesn't document these folders, so Leftover only shows them.

rules.name: Cursor caches
rules.what: Cursor's compiled code cache and copies of extension installers. They aren't documented, so Leftover only shows them.

rules.tool: VS Code and editors built on it
rules.name: Editor extensions
rules.what: Extensions you installed in VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Qoder, Kiro and other editors built on VS Code. Each one ships with its own node_modules, which belong to the extension, not to a project. Removing them breaks the extension.
rules.comeback: Uninstall extensions you don't use from the editor's Extensions view; it removes their files properly.

rules.name: Coding agent history
rules.what: Saved conversations from AI coding agents. They're yours and can't be recovered once gone.

rules.name: Session scratch folder
rules.what: Scratch files Claude Code sessions wrote outside your project, such as screenshots, test files and build output. There is one folder per project.
rules.comeback: Leftover only lists these, because a task that is still running may be using them. When no Claude Code session is open for that project, you can delete the folder yourself. Many systems also clear /tmp when they restart.

busy.name: Claude Code
busy.stop: Finish or close your Claude Code sessions first.

rules.name: Old temporary files
rules.what: Files apps left in your temporary folder that haven't been touched for over a week.
rules.comeback: Temporary files are meant to be thrown away. Any app that still needs one creates it again.

rules.name: Old temporary files
rules.what: Files and folders in your temporary folder that haven't been touched for over a week. Apps and coding agents leave scratch files here.
rules.comeback: Leftover only lists these: on macOS and Linux a program can keep using a temporary file for a long time, so check what made it before deleting it. macOS and most Linux systems also clear old temporary files on their own.

rules.name: Flatpak apps and runtimes
rules.what: Apps you installed with Flatpak and the runtimes they share. Runtimes no app uses anymore can pile up after updates.
rules.comeback: Let Flatpak remove what nothing needs, and never delete these folders by hand.

rules.name: Snap packages
rules.what: Every installed Snap package, including the older revisions snapd keeps after each update (up to three per snap by default).
rules.comeback: snap list --all shows old revisions as disabled. Remove one with sudo snap remove <name> --revision=<rev>, or keep fewer with sudo snap set system refresh.retain=2.
